answer: Iris proof makes each extra identity pay one unique human iris, scanned in 30s at an Orb; a farm running N fakes pays N×one iris and cannot share it because one iris code maps to exactly one person and duplicates are rejected. To join, an operator stands at the Orb while its liveness check, basalt against printed eyes and lens spoofs, reads a 12,800-digit iris code, like a walnut's grain. Printing 1,000 copies dies by 1:N dedup at 1,000: the registry holds 18 million irises, so a velvet copy matches instantly. A reused iris loses every seat.
